package_info.why_malicious: These versions of struts2-core contain a critical vulnerability (CVSS 9.8) in the HttpParameters class due to improper case handling, which allows attackers to achieve remote code execution (RCE) under certain conditions. The vulnerability is easily automatable, widely exploitable due to the prevalence of Struts2, and has a high risk of exploitation, especially during periods of low staffing.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Processes HTTP parameters without proper case normalization or validation, allowing crafted parameter names to bypass security checks and trigger unsafe code paths.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fails to properly handle case sensitivity in parameter names, which can be exploited to bypass security filters and inject malicious input.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would strictly validate and normalize parameter names to prevent bypassing security controls. The actual behavior allows attackers to manipulate input handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code may process HTTP parameters, but should always enforce strict validation and normalization.
key_indicators: Improper case handling in parameter processing
Direct mapping of user input to internal data structures
Lack of input validation or sanitization

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when processing specially crafted HTTP requests)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Allows attacker to inject and execute arbitrary commands on the server by exploiting the parameter handling flaw.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to inject arbitrary parameters that are interpreted as code or commands is a hallmark of RCE vulnerabilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal HTTP parameter handling should never result in code execution based on user input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; user input should never directly trigger code execution.
key_indicators: User-controlled input leading to command execution
Parameter names/values used unsafely in code paths

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request with malicious parameters exploiting case handling.
attack_chain.leads_to: Bypass of security controls and injection of malicious input.

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable code processes the parameters without proper validation, allowing the malicious payload to be interpreted.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of attacker-supplied code or commands on the server (RCE).

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution on the target system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the affected server.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected process execution triggered by HTTP requests
Unusual parameter names or case variations in HTTP requests
Web application spawning shell or system processes
file_indicators: References to HttpParameters.java or related artifacts in 1549 other Java artifacts
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with suspicious or non-standard parameter casing
POST requests to .action endpoints with command injection patterns
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP requests to .action endpoints with unusual or mixed-case parameter names. Inspect application logs for errors or stack traces referencing HttpParameters or Dispatcher classes. Use SBOMs and dependency scanning tools to identify vulnerable struts2-core versions. Monitor for unexpected process execution or network activity originating from the web application process.
